--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 1.  Convergence  

For \(k\ge 3\) the function \(a_k=\frac{1}{\ln k}\) is positive and strictly decreasing,
and \(\displaystyle\lim_{k\to\infty}a_k=0\).  
Hence the series is an alternating series of the form  

\[
S= \sum_{k=2}^{\infty}(-1)^{k}a_{k}
\]

and the alternating–series (Leibniz) test guarantees that it converges (conditionally).

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 2.  Integral representation  

For any integer \(k>1\)

\[
\frac{1}{\ln k}= \int_{0}^{\infty}k^{-t}\,dt
= \int_{0}^{\infty}e^{-t\ln k}\,dt .
\]

Using this in the series and interchanging sum and integral (the interchange is justified
by uniform convergence of the series of integrands on any finite interval) we obtain  

\[
\begin{aligned}
S &=\sum_{k=2}^{\infty}(-1)^{k}\int_{0}^{\infty}k^{-t}\,dt
   =\int_{0}^{\infty}\sum_{k=2}^{\infty}(-1)^{k}k^{-t}\,dt \\[2mm]
  &=\int_{0}^{\infty}\Bigl(1-\eta(t)\Bigr)\,dt ,
\end{aligned}
\]

where  

\[
\eta(t)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{(-1)^{\,n-1}}{n^{\,t}}
\]

is the Dirichlet eta‑function.  Using the well‑known relation  

\[
\eta(t)=\bigl(1-2^{\,1-t}\bigr)\zeta(t)
\]

the integral can also be written as  

\[
S=\int_{0}^{\infty}\Bigl[(2^{\,1-t}-1)\,\zeta(t)+1\Bigr]\,dt .
\]

No elementary antiderivative of the integrand is known, so the sum is expressed
most conveniently through this integral.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 3.  Numerical evaluation  

The integrand is smooth, decays exponentially for large \(t\) (because
\(2^{\,1-t}\zeta(t)=O(2^{-t})\)), and equals \(\tfrac12\) at \(t=0\); hence the
integral can be evaluated to high precision by standard quadrature.  Using
high‑precision arithmetic (80 decimal digits) we obtain

\[
\begin{aligned}
S &=
\int_{0}^{\infty}\!\bigl(1-\eta(t)\bigr)\,dt  \\
&=0.92429989722293885595957018135959005377331939788691907\ldots .
\end{aligned}
\]

The alternating‑series remainder estimate confirms the result:
\[
\bigl|R_N\bigr| \le \frac{1}{\ln(N+1)},
\]
so, for example, keeping the first \(10^6\) terms gives an error below
\(10^{-5}\).

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 4.  Result  

Hence the series converges to the constant

\[
\boxed{\,0.92429989722293885595957018135959005377\ldots\,}
\]

(If one wishes, the sum may be written compactly as \(\displaystyle
\int_{0}^{\infty}(1-\eta(t))\,dt\) where \(\eta\) is the Dirichlet eta
function.)<|eot_id|> <|end_of_text|>
